chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah curse those who block the paths of kindness.' It was said, 'And what are those who block the paths of kindness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man receives a favor, but he fails to appreciate it, so the provider of the favor refrains from doing that same favor to others.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُهُ: The provider / The one who gave the favor
key_terms.قَاطِعِي سُبُلِ الْمَعْرُوفِ: Those who block the paths of kindness
key_terms.يَكْفُرُهُ: He fails to appreciate it / He is ungrateful for it

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to block the path of kindness in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to define 'blocking the path of kindness' (qaati' subul al-ma'ruf) as ingratitude that causes the giver to withhold future favors from others, thereby stifling social generosity. This concept is central to Shia ethical teachings on maintaining communal bonds, illustrating how individual ingratitude has a ripple effect that diminishes collective well-being and discourages the continuous flow of benevolence within the community.
